newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French Pallas Stern bond holders unhappy on rescue.
newsitem.headline: French Pallas Stern bond holders unhappy on rescue.

text.p: Holders of bonds issued by French Bank Pallas Stern (BPS) are unhappy with present plans to liquidate the bank, according to reports of a meeting held in Luxembourg on Wednesday.

"The (bond holders) consider that the contribution by (BPS) shareholders that is presently foreseen in the plans is unsatisfactory compared to the size of the shortfall in assets," the bond holders said in a statement, issued by the Luxembourg auditors who oversaw the meeting.

They said, however, they would take a favorable view on any "improved plan" that offered them a higher dividend, liquid tradeable securities in lieu of payment, or a plan which contained more asset sales and the support of BPS shareholders.

A Paris commercial court is due to rule by February 28 on various possible bailout plans for BPS, which include the merger with its parent Comipar, which is also in receivership, and/or a takeover, or to declare BPS bankrupt.

BPS filed for creditor protection in June 1995. It later emerged its main shareholder Comipar owed it some 3.5 billion Belgian francs. Comipar filed for bankruptcy in February 1996 when the court overseeing the liquidation of BPS ordered it to immediately pay at least 2.6 billion francs of the debt.
Among creditors owed money by BPS are Belgian chemical group Solvay, Belgian newspaper De Financieel Economische Tijd reported last year.
